name: Sulfur soap

card.summary: A bar soap containing sulfur, popular in Japan and the Philippines, used to clear breakouts and oily skin for a clearer complexion.
card.note: Sulfur products can dry or irritate skin and have a noticeable odour.

quick.overview:
Sulfur soap is a cleansing bar made with precipitated or colloidal sulfur. Sulfur has a long history as a topical agent, with antifungal, antibacterial and keratolytic (skin-peeling) properties, and it has been used for acne, rosacea, seborrheic dermatitis and dandruff.[1]

People use sulfur soap for a clearer complexion: it helps remove oil and dead skin and is applied to breakouts. Soaps are one of the pharmaceutical forms in which sulfur is sold.[1]
quick.how: Users wash the face or body with the bar like ordinary soap. It is a cleanser with sulfur rather than a leave-on treatment. It sometimes appears in skin-care routines alongside other acne products.
quick.risks: Sulfur is described as keratolytic, which can lead to dryness and peeling, and sulfur products have a characteristic smell. This page does not provide medical guidance, and people with skin conditions are usually advised to consult a clinician.

lead: Sulfur soap is a soap bar containing sulfur, used for acne-prone and oily skin. Sulfur has been used topically for a long time and is considered to have antifungal, antibacterial and keratolytic properties.[1]

Historical and current topical uses of sulfur include acne, rosacea, seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff, pityriasis versicolor and scabies. Precipitated and colloidal sulfur appear in lotions, creams, powders, soaps and bath additives.[1] Its exact mechanism is unclear but is thought to involve hydrogen sulfide and other antifungal compounds forming on skin.[1]

The bar has a following in Japan and the Philippines as an acne soap. One 2025 case report from a clinical setting mentions sulfur soap among topical agents used alongside tea tree oil wash and oral metronidazole after surgery for a rare Demodex folliculorum nipple infestation, which is a medical case rather than a cosmetic use.[2]

chain: Wash skin with a sulfur-containing bar
Sulfur loosens dead skin and acts on bacteria and fungi
Fewer breakouts and a clearer, less oily surface
angle.text: Users wash with sulfur soap to reduce oil and breakouts. It exfoliates lightly through sulfur's keratolytic action.

paras: Sulfur soaps are used for acne and oily skin, and the same ingredient is used in treating seborrheic dermatitis and dandruff.[1] Scabies and ringworm are also treated with sulfur preparations.[1]

The Ebers Papyrus records ancient Egyptians using a sulfur ointment for granular eyelids.[1] Sulfur was a staple remedy through the centuries and appeared in 19th-century tonics and in Madam C. J. Walker's hair products in the early 1900s.[1]

No studies found on sulfur soap bars as an acne treatment. A 2025 case report notes sulfur soap as one topical agent used with oral metronidazole after surgery for Demodex folliculorum infestation of the nipple.[2] Studies of other topical sulfur products appear under the Sulfur (topical) entry.
